title: Speech processors, S meters, band edges
blurb: Explain what a speech processor changes, how S-meter steps relate to power, and where your SSB signal sits near a band edge.

G4D01.why: Compression raises the average voice level, so the signal sounds **louder** without raising the peak limit.
G4D01.trap: It doesn't add bass, limit bandwidth or prevent distortion.

G4D02.why: The peak is capped by the transmitter, but compressing raises the quieter parts, so **average power rises**.
G4D02.trap: Processing doesn't lift the peak. Too much makes intermodulation worse.

G4D03.why: Over-processing flattens peaks, giving **distorted speech**, intermodulation products and raised background noise: **all of these**.

G4D04.why: An S meter reads the **strength of the received signal** at the receiver.
G4D04.trap: Transmitter power and impedance need other meters.

G4D05.why: Power ratio = 10^(20 ÷ 10) = 10² = **100 times** the S9 signal.
G4D05.trap: 20 dB is not 20 times: dB is logarithmic.

G4D06.why: One S unit is **6 dB**, so each S unit is about a 4× change in power.

G4D07.why: S8 to S9 is one S unit, 6 dB. Power ratio = 10^(6 ÷ 10) ≈ **4 times**.
G4D07.trap: 6 dB is not double. +3 dB doubles power, +6 dB quadruples.

G4D08.why: LSB extends **below** the carrier: 7.178 − 0.003 = **7.175 to 7.178 MHz**.
G4D08.trap: That range above the carrier is USB.

G4D09.why: USB extends **above** the carrier: 14.347 + 0.003 = **14.347 to 14.350 MHz**.

G4D10.why: LSB extends 3 kHz down, so the carrier must sit **at least 3 kHz above** the lower edge.
G4D10.trap: Below the edge puts the carrier outside the segment.

G4D11.why: USB extends 3 kHz up, so the carrier must sit **at least 3 kHz below** the upper edge.
G4D11.trap: Above the edge puts the carrier outside the segment.
